attestations.source_text: In direct speech (le discours direct), one says something or asks a question directly. ... In indirect speech (le discours indirect), the words of one or more people are reported or a question is asked indirectly.

sections.title: Main clause verbs in indirect speech

attestations.section_title: Main clause verbs in indirect speech
attestations.source_text: Verbs in the main clause of indirect speech are followed by que (où, si, etc.); the verb in the dependent clause is usually in the indicative. Here are some typical main clause verbs: affirmer, annoncer, assurer, avouer, confier, constater, crier, déclarer, dire, expliquer, observer, prétendre, promettre, remarquer, répondre, révéler, s'apercevoir, savoir, se rendre compte.

sections.title: Balancing tenses: la concordance des temps

attestations.section_title: Balancing tenses: la concordance des temps
attestations.source_text: Learning la concordance des temps, that is, balancing tenses, is one of the most difficult tasks of a French learner. When switching from direct to indirect speech, some changes of tense occur when the main clause verb is in the passé composé.
If the direct speech is in the present tense, the dependent clause verb is changed into the imparfait.

sections.title: Passé composé recounted in the plus-que-parfait

attestations.section_title: Passé composé recounted in the plus-que-parfait
attestations.source_text: If the direct speech is in the passé composé, the verb in the dependent clause is changed into the plus-que-parfait.

sections.title: Future recounted in the present conditional

attestations.section_title: Future recounted in the present conditional
attestations.source_text: If the direct speech is in the future, the dependent clause verb is changed into the conditionnel in the indirect speech.

grammar_rules.summary: Indirect speech reports words or questions without quotation marks, using a main clause verb followed by que, où, si, etc.
grammar_rules.explanation: In indirect speech, the words of one or more people are reported or a question is asked indirectly. There are no quotation marks.
grammar_rules.formation: Main clause verb + que / où / si / etc. + dependent clause
usage: To relate conversational exchanges or information in the third person
conditions: The verb in the dependent clause is usually in the indicative

attestations.source_text: In indirect speech, the words of one or more people are reported or a question is asked indirectly. There are no quotation marks.

grammar_rules.rule_name: Main clause verbs followed by que
grammar_rules.summary: Verbs in the main clause of indirect speech are followed by que (où, si, etc.); the dependent clause is usually indicative.
grammar_rules.explanation: A list of typical main clause verbs is provided: affirmer, annoncer, assurer, avouer, confier, constater, crier, déclarer, dire, expliquer, observer, prétendre, promettre, remarquer, répondre, révéler, s'apercevoir, savoir, se rendre compte.
grammar_rules.formation: [main clause verb] + que / où / si + [dependent clause in indicative]

grammar_rules.rule_name: Present tense in main clause: no tense change
grammar_rules.summary: If the main clause verb is in the present tense, the dependent clause verb remains in the same tense as in direct speech.
grammar_rules.formation: Main clause present + dependent clause same tense
usage: When reporting speech with present tense main clause
conditions: Main clause verb is in present tense

attestations.source_text: If the verb in the main clause is in the present tense, the verb in the dependent clause remains in the same tense as it is in the direct speech.

grammar_rules.summary: If the main clause verb is in passé composé and direct speech is in present, change the dependent verb to imparfait.
grammar_rules.formation: Main clause passé composé + dependent verb imparfait
usage: When reporting present tense statements with a past main clause
conditions: Direct speech is in present tense
Main clause is in passé composé
